transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been really slowed down. At work, I can sit there staring at one audit workpaper for twenty minutes before I even move my hand to type. People have started noticing I’m not keeping up.
Have you been feeling depressed?
Yes. Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest… like the day is already lost before I’ve even gotten out of bed.
Have you been hearing voices that other people can’t hear?
Yes. Sometimes when I open a spreadsheet or my email, I hear a clear voice, like it’s coming from just behind my laptop. It says, “You missed it, they know,” even when I’m alone in the room.
Have you heard that voice at times when you were not feeling depressed?

No, I don’t think so. I never heard that voice before I got this low. The idea that the firm was secretly building a case against me… that started after my mood and energy had already been bad for a while.
Before this current period, have you ever had another episode in your life where you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had times before where I felt down or stressed, but I can’t clearly say there was another stretch like this that lasted two weeks or more.
Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally energized or unusually up, not just less depressed?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt a little better or got through a busy period, but not abnormally energized or unusually up like that.
Does the voice say things that fit with feeling guilty, worthless, or deserving punishment?

Yes, kind of. When I open a spreadsheet or my email, sometimes I hear this clear voice, like it’s coming from just behind my laptop, saying, “You missed it, they know.” It makes me feel like I’ve done something wrong and I’m going to be found out.
When you hear that voice, do you recognize it as your own thoughts, or does it seem like an external voice speaking to you?
It doesn’t feel like my own thoughts. It feels like an actual voice, like it’s outside of me, coming from behind my laptop, even when I’m alone in the room.
How long have you been feeling this depressed?
About seven months, I think. It started around when my husband stopped working after the downsizing, and it’s just kind of kept going since then.
Besides the voice, do you firmly believe that your firm is secretly building a case against you?

Yes. I know people keep telling me that’s not happening—my husband shows me the bank balance, and my manager says my job isn’t in danger—but I still feel certain I’ve already ruined us financially. And I can’t shake the thought that the firm is quietly collecting things to prove I’m incompetent and expose me.
Do you feel certain that you have already ruined your family financially?

Yes. I know it doesn’t make sense to other people, and my husband keeps showing me the account balance, but I still feel sure I’ve already destroyed everything financially. I can’t get that certainty out of my head.
Before this seven-month period, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think there was anything like this before, at least not that I remember lasting that long every day.
Have you ever had a time when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve had trouble sleeping, but I don’t remember ever needing less sleep and still feeling energized.
